web_evidence.title: Revisiting Stephen King: A Critical Companion
web_evidence.note: Published scholarly structural analysis states that point of view shifts across the five stories; it identifies “Low Men in Yellow Coats” as limited third person and the title novella as first person.

web_evidence.title: Hearts in Atlantis by Stephen King
web_evidence.note: The contemporary review explicitly contrasts the third-person narration of “Low Men” with the first-person narration of “Hearts” and notes differing styles among the narratives.

web_evidence.title: Shell-Shocked
web_evidence.note: The Washington Post explicitly describes the novella “Hearts in Atlantis,” narrated by Pete Riley, as a first-person story.

web_evidence.title: Book Review: Hearts in Atlantis – by Stephen King
web_evidence.note: A detailed whole-book review identifies Parts 1, 3, 4, and 5 as third person and Part 2 as Pete's first-person account.

person_note: The book alternates narrative person across five sustained, interconnected sections. The scholarly structural analysis and independent reviews agree that “Low Men in Yellow Coats” and the later stories use third-person narration while Pete Riley narrates the substantial title novella in first person. The quote sample independently contains diagnostic first-person narration and sustained third-person passages. Generic you, aphoristic I/we, dialogue, and local thought were not promoted to base-person evidence. No credible source indicated sustained second-person narration or contradicted the alternating structure.
